arms.label: Experiment 1: social media / university panel invitations (mostly British), 2 x 2 x 2 between

cite.label: reported
cite.note: 'A total of 404 people responded to invitations distributed on social media, and by email to a university psychology student participant panel'

arms.exclusion_caveat: the paper's exclusions cannot be replayed: 72 (17.8%) who did not start or gave no relevant data (a participant-side event); 21 (5.2%) who reported not understanding the vignette / questions (their question's wording is not printed); 4 (1.0%) who asked for their data not to be used (a choice outside the task); 7 (1.7%) whose 'two or all three of their judgments were outliers' (no threshold printed). 404 - 72 - 21 - 4 - 7 = 300

exclusion_caveat_cite.label: reported
exclusion_caveat_cite.note: '72 (17.8%) did not start the questionnaire or provided no relevant data, and 21 (5.2%) reported not properly understanding the vignette and/or questions. assignment.note: 'The order of scenarios and of questions about Garmess, and the version of the Garmess vignette (according to the outcome, weapon type and testimonial or factual version) presented to each participant were allocated randomly and equally' (p. 6, Exp. 1)

assignment_reading.label: derived
assignment_reading.note: the vignette version: 'randomly and equally' read as a balanced draw over the 8 cells (equal cell sizes, Qualtrics EvenPresentation style). Alternative: independent uniform draws (equal in expectation, unequal cells). The realised weapon split after exclusions was 140 / 160 (df of the simple-effect tests, p. 6), so the printed groups were not equal

assignment_e2.label: derived
assignment_e2.note: Exp. 2 prints no assignment rule ('The two main differences from Experiment 1' concern the levels, p. 10). Served as for Exp. 1 (balanced over the 6 cells). Alternative: independent uniform draws. The realised weapon split after exclusions was 81 / 82 / 78 (df of the simple-effect tests, p. 10)

question_order.label: reported
question_order.note: 'The order of scenarios and of questions about Garmess ... were allocated randomly and equally' (p. 6)

question_order_reading.label: derived
question_order_reading.note: a random order of the questions per participant (independent permutation, shuffle_responses). Unlike the 8 cells, 'equally' cannot be served as balanced over orders: no set of orders is printed (120 permutations of five questions). Alternative: balanced over a fixed unprinted set of orders

position.label: reported
